inline_comments.comment: `createLabel` is `async`, so this call returns a Promise, not a DOM element. Without `await`, `label` is a Promise object — `elem.node().appendChild(label)` will throw a TypeError and `label.getBBox()` will never be reached. This function needs to be made `async` and the call needs `await`: `const label = await createLabel(...)`. Note: the dagre-wrapper counterpart (`dagre-wrapper/clusters.js`) correctly uses `async`/`await` for the same pattern.

`style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` will throw a TypeError if `style` is `undefined` or `null`. The HTML label path above correctly guards against this with `style ? style.replace('fill:', 'color:') : style`, but the SVG path has no equivalent null check. Apply the same guard here: `style ? style.replace('color:', 'fill:') : ''`.

Same issue as in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`: `style.replace('color:', 'fill:')` will throw a TypeError if `style` is `undefined` or `null`. The HTML path above already handles this correctly with `style ? style.replace('fill:', 'color:') : style`; the SVG path needs the same guard.

`useHtmlLabels` is being passed as the `addBackground` argument. These are semantically unrelated: `useHtmlLabels` indicates whether HTML rendering is globally enabled, while `addBackground` controls whether a `labelBkg` CSS class is added to the label's div. As written, every edge label will silently receive `class="labelBkg"` whenever HTML labels are enabled system-wide, regardless of whether a background is actually desired for that label. These concerns should be kept separate — either derive `addBackground` from edge-specific data, or default it to a constant `true`/`false` as appropriate.

Same DOM leak issue as in `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`: `tempSvg` is appended to `document.body` but is only removed on the success path. If an exception is thrown inside the measurement block, the hidden SVG element is never cleaned up. Use a `try/finally` block to guarantee `tempSvg.remove()` is always called.

`edge.width || getConfig().flowchart?.wrappingWidth` uses `||`, which treats a valid width of `0` as falsy and falls back to the config value unintentionally. Use the nullish coalescing operator instead: `edge.width ?? getConfig().flowchart?.wrappingWidth`.

`getConfig()` is called twice in the same `setupImage` function (lines 34–35). Since config is not expected to change mid-call, cache the result once: `const config = getConfig(); const bodyFontSize = config.fontSize ? config.fontSize : window.getComputedStyle(document.body).fontSize;`.

The log level was changed from `log.debug` to `log.info` for a routine intermediate value trace. `info`-level messages are typically visible in production environments, so printing the full `vertexText` string at that level can be unexpectedly noisy. This should remain `log.debug`.

general_comments.comment: The PR description states the goal is to reduce duplication by making `createLabel` delegate to `createText`. However, the actual implementation duplicates the newly-refactored `addHtmlLabel` function, `getWrappingWidth`, and `DEFAULT_WRAPPING_WIDTH` verbatim across two separate files: `dagre-wrapper/createLabel.js` and `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js`. Any future bug fix or behavior change will need to be applied in both places. Consider extracting the shared `addHtmlLabel` into a common utility (e.g., alongside `labelImageUtils.ts`) and importing it into both `createLabel` files.

Two new CSS styles — `line-height: 1.5` and `text-align: center` — have been added to `addHtmlLabel` in both `createLabel.js` files without any accompanying comment or changelog note. These are visual behavior changes that will affect all existing diagrams using these label paths. It's worth documenting why these values were chosen, and whether this constitutes a visual breaking change that needs a minor-version bump rather than a patch.

The `padding-right: 1px` style present in the old `rendering-util/rendering-elements/createLabel.js` was silently removed without any comment. Given it was originally added to address a layout edge case, its removal warrants a brief explanation (e.g., "no longer needed because the foreignObject is now explicitly sized") so future readers understand the intent.

The initial foreignObject dimensions are set to the magic number `10000` (e.g., `fo.attr('width', 10000).attr('height', 10000)`) in both `createLabel.js` files. This value should be extracted into a named constant (e.g., `const LARGE_DIMENSION = 10000`) with a brief comment explaining its purpose — to give the browser enough layout space to render the content before the real bounding box is measured.
